evidence: Quint. 9.3.45: initia et clausulae sententiārum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A thought put into words, and so a sentence (Lewis & Short); also an opinion, a vote, a maxim. Sentence by sentence, per singulās sententiās; to answer in full sentences, tōtīs sententiīs respondēre (Traupman 27, 28).

terms.gloss: a period, a long rounded sentence
terms.comment: The orator’s rounded sentence, for which Cicero also says ambitus, circuitus, comprehēnsiō (Or. 204, Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: est brevitāte opus, ut currat sententia, neu sē inpediat verbīs lassās onerantibus aurīs
phrases.english: you need brevity, so that the sentence runs on and does not get tangled in words that weigh on tired ears

phrases.latin: ita verba in variīs sententiīs locīs suīs posita et crēbrō audīta quārum rērum signa essent paulātim conligēbam
phrases.english: so, hearing words again and again, each in its place in different sentences, little by little I worked out what things they stood for
